title: Continuation Failure Classification and Recovery Boundaries
purpose: Classify continuation failure modes and define the boundary between diagnostic failure, recoverable failure, and non-recoverable undefined composition.
core_claim: ⊥C is the general diagnostic continuation-failure marker; typed subclasses refine why the continuation failed without creating lawful continuation objects.

canonical_claims.statement: ⊥C is the general diagnostic continuation-failure marker.
Typed failure classes refine ⊥C without creating lawful continuation objects.
Failure classification records why continuation failed.
Classification is diagnostic and does not itself recover continuation.
Recovery requires an explicit future recovery rule and is not automatic.

formal_objects.name: Continuation Failure Classification
formal_objects.definition: Diagnostic classification of continuation failure into endpoint, type, admissibility, and residue subclasses.

failure_classes.name: Type Failure
failure_classes.meaning: Failure caused by incompatible typed continuation domains without an explicit transition rule.

failure_classes.name: Admissibility Failure
failure_classes.meaning: Failure caused by violation of admissibility constraints.

failure_classes.name: Residue Failure
failure_classes.meaning: Failure caused by invalid residue propagation.

recovery_boundaries.meaning: Classifying failure never creates a lawful continuation.
Failure classes do not normalize into continuation normal forms.

validation_requirements: Failure classes registered as diagnostic subclasses of ⊥C.
No failure class is treated as a lawful continuation.

next_recommended_patch.title: Continuation Recovery Operator
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Define the first governed recovery operator for continuation failure subclasses, if and only if a recovery semantics patch is authorized.
